transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-05
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Jared (CTO - Orion), Priya (Head of Security), Samir (Platform), Lina (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be rough): Customer wants to understand Redwood security controls, compliance artifacts, and how keys/data are handled in Hosted vs Dedicated and Private deployments. Also asked about SSO/SAML flows and audit log retention.

[00:00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you taking the time. Quick intros?
[00:00:07] Jared (Orion): Jared here, CTO, I'll lead on architecture but Priya is our security owner.
[00:00:11] Priya (Orion): Hey all, Priya, Head of Security. Main topics: SOC2 / ISO, SSO, RBAC, auditability, KMS.
[00:00:17] Maya (Redwood): Great. Ethan from our infra team will cover the technical pieces.
[00:00:21] Ethan (Redwood): Hi, thanks. I'll jump in on the deployment options and KMS bits.

[00:00:35] Priya: Big one for us is whether using Hosted means we lose control of keys. We need to know about encryption at rest and if Redwood manages keys or if we can bring our own.
[00:00:50] Ethan: Short answer: Hosted uses Redwoods managed keys by default; we also support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private. For hosted we can do a bring-your-own-key (BYOK) flow through cloud KMS with additional contract terms — but caveat, the private control-plane pattern is strongest for key ownership.
[00:01:12] Priya: When you say BYOK for hosted, is that envelope encryption or full disk? What's the model?
[00:01:20] Ethan: It's envelope encryption. We store model artifacts and KV caches encrypted using a data encryption key (DEK) wrapped by your KMS CMK. So you can rotate keys on your side and we respect that. There are some service account perms we need.
[00:01:33] Priya: Okay, can you show an IAM policy sample?
[00:01:37] Ethan: I'll include a sample in the follow-up — it'll show the minimal permissions we request for key use.

[00:01:55] Samir (Orion): On Dedicated vs Private: what's the difference for audit logs and retention? We need logs retained for 7 years for some data flows.
[00:02:04] Maya: Right — hosted has standard log retention windows (configurable up to 90 days by default for our analytics console) but for longer-term retention you can export audit logs to S3 or your SIEM. Dedicated gives you greater control and we can set longer retention or ship directly to your logging infra. Private (on-prem/VPC) keeps logs in your environment entirely.
[00:02:26] Priya: So with Hosted we rely on Redwood to ship logs to S3? Is that push or can Orion pull logs?
[00:02:31] Ethan: Both patterns exist. We typically offer push exports to your storage via a signed role; you can also query via API and pull. For compliance we recommend push to your vaulted S3 with lifecycle rules.

[00:02:55] [Minor crosstalk] Lina (Orion): sorry - procurement note - are there extra charges for log exports?
[00:03:01] Maya: There can be egress/storage costs depending on volume; we'll include a sizing/pricing estimate.

[00:03:20] Priya: On SSO — we use Okta and SCIM provisioning. We need SAML for SSO and SCIM for group sync to enforce RBAC. How do you support groups mapping?
[00:03:30] Ethan: We support SAML 2.0 and SCIM 2.0. You can map Okta groups to Redwood roles. We support custom roles — so you can have least-privilege roles and map them via SCIM group attributes.
[00:03:41] Priya: Is there an audit trail when an admin changes role mappings?
[00:03:45] Maya: Yes — admin actions are logged in the audit trail with actor identity, timestamp, and the change payload. Those logs are available in the Console and can be exported.

[00:04:02] Jared: What's the model for data residency? Our EU customers' PII must stay in EU. Can Redwood ensure model inference for those requests stays in-region?
[00:04:12] Ethan: We support region routing. For Hosted we run in multiple regions; you can mark requests to route to eu-west-1 endpoints or restrict model serving to regional pools. Dedicated gives you region isolation for committed capacity. Private is fully in your VPC/region.
[00:04:28] Priya: If we route to EU region, are backups replicated elsewhere? That's an issue for our policy.
[00:04:36] Ethan: By default we replicate for HA within the region. Cross-region replication is opt-in and we can disable cross-region backups for EU-only datasets in a Private or Dedicated setup. Hosted default may replicate within the same geo-cluster; we'll include specifics in the compliance doc.

[00:04:58] Samir: For RBAC and multitenancy — we plan to host multiple internal teams and want strict isolation per tenant. Is tenant data logically separated?
[00:05:06] Maya: We have both logical multi-tenancy with strict scoping via namespaces and physical isolation options in Dedicated/Private. For strict regulatory needs, Dedicated with tenant-level VLANs or Private on-prem is recommended.

[00:05:28] Priya: Audit logs — retention, immutability, and ability to prove non-repudiation?
[00:05:34] Ethan: Audit logs have write-once semantics in our internal pipeline and we can provide signed hash chains for attestation upon request under enterprise contracts. For full non-repudiation we recommend shipping logs to your own immutable storage (S3 with Object Lock) — we can automate that export.

[00:05:58] [00:06:00] Priya: SOC2 — is Redwood SOC2 Type II? Can we get the report under NDA?
[00:06:07] Maya: Yes, Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certifications. We'll send the attestation and the certs post-call.
[00:06:14] Priya: Any outstanding exceptions in the latest report we should know about?
[00:06:19] Maya: No major exceptions — we'll share the cover letter and summary. If you want specifics we can schedule a doc walk.

[00:06:36] Jared: For legal — data retention policies in the contract — can we set deletion windows per dataset?
[00:06:43] Maya: Yes, you can set retention and we support TTLs and explicit deletion APIs. For Hosted, deletion requests go through our pipeline; we provide deletion confirmations and audit entries. For Private, it's fully in your control.

[00:07:05] Samir: Technical deep dive request: we want to run a bench with a 512‑token average sequence, 150 qps, 99th-p95 latency SLO of <200 ms for small models. Is that realistic on Dedicated?
[00:07:17] Ethan: Sounds doable with Dedicated and right GPU profiles; we'll need model details and warm KV cache expectations. We'll scope a pilot with those numbers.

[00:07:33] Priya: KMS rotation process — if we rotate keys, what's the exposure window? How fast can you swap wrapped keys?
[00:07:40] Ethan: Key rotation is immediate for new writes; for existing encrypted artifacts we rewrap lazily or you can trigger a rewrap job. We provide migration tooling; speed depends on dataset size. For KV cache keys it's a smaller surface.

[00:07:58] Lina: procurement: do we need a separate addendum to enforce key control?
[00:08:03] Maya: Typically for BYOK and certain data residency requirements we sign a security addendum (SDA) or bring-your-own-key addendum. I'll surface a template.

[00:08:20] [00:08:22] Priya: About pen tests — does Redwood run annual pen tests? Can we see results or a summary?
[00:08:28] Maya: Yes, annual third-party assessments; we can share the summary report and remediation timelines under NDA.

[00:08:40] Samir: Regarding network topology for Private — can we do direct fiber / cross connect or is it just VPC peering?
[00:08:47] Ethan: Private supports VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink, and in some regions partner direct connect options. Cross-connects to co-lo sites are possible with our private deployment package.

[00:09:05] Priya: Can we have a dedicated control plane but still have inference in our VPC? We want control plane logs not to leave our tenancy.
[00:09:13] Ethan: We offer a private control plane option that can be customer-hosted; that keeps control-plane metadata in your environment. For hybrid we can run the data plane in your VPC and the control plane in a restricted customer-managed tenancy. We'll include diagrams.

[00:09:32] Jared: Any downtime SLA for Dedicated?
[00:09:36] Maya: Dedicated comes with an SLA, typically 99.9% based on reserved capacity; enterprise tiers can go higher. We'll share the SLA table.

[00:09:50] Lina: procurement follow-up: what's typical commitment length for Dedicated?
[00:09:54] Maya: 12 or 36 month commitments are common; we offer monthly burst capacity.

[00:10:10] [A few clarifying q's and some small interruptions omitted for brevity]

[00:12:14] Ethan: I'll call out one nuance — hosted BYOK has more limited guarantees around key escrow since Redwood still runs the control plane. For full key sovereignty we recommend Dedicated with CMK integration or Private where the control plane is on-prem.

[00:12:40] Priya: What about data plane logs for inference prompts — we have regulatory restrictions on PII; can you redact or avoid storing prompts altogether?
[00:12:50] Maya: We support prompt redaction at ingestion and selective logging. For strict PII scenarios we can turn off request logging for specific routes and only keep aggregate metrics. This is easier on Dedicated/Private.

[00:13:06] Samir: Schema: do you log full prompts for analytics or just token counts?
[00:13:12] Ethan: By default we keep request/response traces for debugging with redaction rules; you can configure to store only metadata. We'll provide the default schema and fields.

[00:13:35] Priya: Are audit logs tamper-evident? You mentioned signed hash chains — can you automate verification?
[00:13:43] Ethan: We can produce signed digests on a cadence and you can verify them. For automated continuous verification we'd recommend shipping to your S3 with Object Lock and running your verifier.

[00:13:58] Jared: Onboarding timeline — if we choose Dedicated, how long to provision capacity?
[00:14:04] Maya: Usually 4–6 weeks for baseline capacity (procurement/contracting dependent). Private on-prem depends on your infra readiness — often 6–12 weeks. Hosted is immediate.

[00:14:20] Priya: For compliance we'd like a pre-demo security workshop where we go through the SOC2 controls mapped to our internal control IDs. Can we do that?
[00:14:27] Maya: Absolutely — that's a reasonable request. We'll schedule a controls-mapping session with our compliance lead.

[00:14:40] [00:15:00] Action recap from Maya: I'll send SOC2/ISO certs, share the KMS/IAM sample, and pricing. Ethan will set up the infra deep dive.

[00:15:15] Priya: One last question: do you support HSM-backed keys (Cloud HSM or external HSM)?
[00:15:21] Ethan: Yes — we integrate with cloud HSM (e.g., AWS CloudHSM) and external HSM via key wrapping; for Private you can use your own HSM.

[00:15:32] Jared: Great — sounds good. We'll review docs and come back with a prioritized list of must-haves.

[00:15:40] Lina: Procurement will want the pricing doc and contract template before 11/07.

[00:15:45] Maya: We'll get that out. Thanks everyone.

[00:15:50] [Call winds down with a few technical clarifications off-line] 

Closing notes (auto): Next steps and action items captured. Red flags: customer insistence on long-term log retention (7 years) and strong key sovereignty; requires Dedicated/Private conversation.

References mentioned (to be attached in follow-up): SOC2 report (link), ISO 27001 cert (link), KMS integration sample policy (link), pricing deck (link), pilot scope template (link).
